content.content: {"result":"{\"documentId\": \"f_3ca9e15d7b20f4e681ad52\", \"title\": \"DD bug carry-over notes\", \"name\": \"DD bug carry-over notes\", \"revisionId\": \"42599f1a8a\", \"createdTime\": \"2026-02-12T22:48:00Z\", \"modifiedTime\": \"2026-02-12T22:48:00Z\", \"text\": \"DD bug carry-over notes\\n\\nWhat goes over: every ticked or unticked line in the comment channel of Vincent's Android canvas, and every bug posted in the bug channel after the last line in that comment channel. A comment whose line was deleted has nothing to carry over. In the bug channel a follow-up on a bug already posted is part of that bug, and a design question for Leonard or a post that points at a QA doc isn't a bug post. Nothing else. Robert's reports in the sub-250 channel aren't part of this, Brian dealt with those at the time. The economy canvas and the ZM canvases stay where they are.\\n\\nOne Linear record per canvas line and one per bug posted after it. A canvas line and a later post stay separate even where they read alike. Take the first outcome that fits.\\nFixed: the tick stands, or a later record says it was fixed. File it as Done.\\nGone: it isn't fixed and it's a bug in something the build players have no longer has. File it as Canceled.\\nCovered: it isn't fixed and an open ticket already covers it. Don't file a new one, add a note on that ticket with the canvas wording. Vincent tied a few lines to tickets before he left.\\nBroken: anything else. File it as Bugs.\\n\\nWhat counts: we go by the Android build players have, 0.3.310, which came off the economy line, not by develop. A tick on the canvas stands unless a later record about that bug says otherwise. An unticked line, or a bug nobody closed, stays open unless a later record says it was fixed, and a commit named for the bug counts as that record if nothing later says otherwise. A fix only counts once it is in that build. A PR that never made it into that build doesn't count.\\n\\nNew tickets: Engineering team, Bug label, parent ENG-2401, title is the line without its tick box, or the first line of the post, as it was written, no assignee, nothing in the description. If anything changes after this I'll put it on the master ticket.\\n\\nUI tree: every open child goes Done unless a record shows a piece of its UI work never made it into that build or the screen is switched off there. Then it stays where it is. Children already Done stay Done and the masters stay as they are. A bug on a screen doesn't hold its child, that's what the bug ticket is for. Brian and Oliver left notes on some of the open children. Brian's closing rule from the UI work applies to the line on every child, Done or not.\\n\\nSheet columns: Bug, Outcome, Ticket, Why. When you report back, Covered ones count as still broken.\\n\"}"}

{"documentId": "f_3ca9e15d7b20f4e681ad52", "title": "DD bug carry-over notes", "name": "DD bug carry-over notes", "revisionId": "42599f1a8a", "createdTime": "2026-02-12T22:48:00Z", "modifiedTime": "2026-02-12T22:48:00Z", "text": "DD bug carry-over notes

What goes over: every ticked or unticked line in the comment channel of Vincent's Android canvas, and every bug posted in the bug channel after the last line in that comment channel. A comment whose line was deleted has nothing to carry over. In the bug channel a follow-up on a bug already posted is part of that bug, and a design question for Leonard or a post that points at a QA doc isn't a bug post. Nothing else. Robert's reports in the sub-250 channel aren't part of this, Brian dealt with those at the time. The economy canvas and the ZM canvases stay where they are.

One Linear record per canvas line and one per bug posted after it. A canvas line and a later post stay separate even where they read alike. Take the first outcome that fits.
Fixed: the tick stands, or a later record says it was fixed. File it as Done.
Gone: it isn't fixed and it's a bug in something the build players have no longer has. File it as Canceled.
Covered: it isn't fixed and an open ticket already covers it. Don't file a new one, add a note on that ticket with the canvas wording. Vincent tied a few lines to tickets before he left.
Broken: anything else. File it as Bugs.

What counts: we go by the Android build players have, 0.3.310, which came off the economy line, not by develop. A tick on the canvas stands unless a later record about that bug says otherwise. An unticked line, or a bug nobody closed, stays open unless a later record says it was fixed, and a commit named for the bug counts as that record if nothing later says otherwise. A fix only counts once it is in that build. A PR that never made it into that build doesn't count.

New tickets: Engineering team, Bug label, parent ENG-2401, title is the line without its tick box, or the first line of the post, as it was written, no assignee, nothing in the description. If anything changes after this I'll put it on the master ticket.

UI tree: every open child goes Done unless a record shows a piece of its UI work never made it into that build or the screen is switched off there. Then it stays where it is. Children already Done stay Done and the masters stay as they are. A bug on a screen doesn't hold its child, that's what the bug ticket is for. Brian and Oliver left notes on some of the open children. Brian's closing rule from the UI work applies to the line on every child, Done or not.

Camera-based UI is affected by URP changes\nWhen the Canvas is set to *Screen Space \u2013 Camera* (or World Space):\n\u2022 UI is rendered *by a Camera*\n\u2022 It goes through the *same render pipeline as the 3D scene*\n\u2022 Disabling *lighting, shadows, or post-processing* changes the camera\u2019s render path\n\u2022 On some Android GPUs, this causes the UI to:\nNot render at all, or\nRender incorrectly (z-order / alpha / depth issues)\nThis is why the bottom bar disappears *only after lighting/shadow changes*.\n\n2. Screen Space \u2013 Overlay fixes UI, but exposes another dependency\nWhen switching to *Screen Space \u2013 Overlay*:\n\u2022 UI is rendered *after the scene*\n\u2022 It bypasses:\nCameras\nLighting\nShadows\nPost-processing\nSo the bottom bar becomes visible again.\nHowever, this also *removes any implicit coupling* between UI and the scene.\n If gameplay visuals (e.g. characters) were *incorrectly relying on camera settings shared with UI*, those issues become visible immediately.\nIn other words:\n> Overlay mode didn\u2019t break character visuals \u2014 it *revealed an existing dependency*.\n3. Why this happens only on some Android devices\nDifferent Android devices use different GPUs (Adreno, Mali, PowerVR), and:\n\u2022 They handle *depth, alpha, and render order* differently\n\u2022 URP shader variants and render passes can behave inconsistently\n\u2022 Some devices fail silently instead of logging errors\nThis is why:\n\u2022 The issue does not reproduce on all devices\n\u2022 It appears specifically after lighting/shadow changes\nKey Takeaway\nThe core problem is *not the UI itself*, but that:\n> *UI and gameplay rendering are incorrectly coupled through the same camera / render pipeline.*\nScreen Space \u2013 Overlay is a *valid fix for UI*, but the character rendering issue indicates *another underlying render dependency* that needs to be separated.", "channel": • The main purpose of showing users their inventory is to make them aware of tokens they might have accumulated without realizing it. However, when we add the inventory to the profile section, I think users have to go through too many steps to access it. As a result, users who are not curious may not frequently check their inventory, leading them to remain unaware of the tokens they've accumulated.
• Additionally, having such an inventory could allow users to make more informed decisions when selecting packages from the store in the future.
Therefore, instead of showing users their inventory directly, I would like to propose the following suggestion:
• We can create a systematic and customizable panel. 
• This panel should be triggered according to the user's inventory and remind them of the tokens they have collected (of course it should be triggered at a certain time period, e.g. once a week).
• For example, a message like “You have collected XX tokens, let's spend them!” could appear with an illustration and direct users to the relevant section with a button on the panel.
• If the user is not interested, they can close the panel and continue playing.
• We could also offer users who close the panel an extra opportunity to trade their tokens later on.", "channel": "C05H8KVNU67", "user": "EMPLOYEE_0026_SLACK_ID", "files": [{"created": 1724164469, "filetype": "png", "id": "F07HQ0ZDZU2", "is_public": false, "mimetype": "image/png", "name": "image.png", "permalink": "https://harmonygamesgroup.slack.com/files/EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID/F07HQ0ZDZU2/image.png", "size": 60116, "timestamp": 1724164469, "title": "image.png", "url_private": "https://files.slack.com/files-pri/T04RZ2JAMM0-F07HQ0ZDZU2/image.png?token=xoxb-REDACTED", "user": "EMPLOYEE_0026_SLACK_ID"}, {"created": 1724164627, "filetype": "png", "id": "F07H9EQPST1", "is_public": false, "mimetype": "image/png", "name": "image.png", "permalink": "https://harmonygamesgroup.slack.com/files/EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID/F07H9EQPST1/image.png", "size": 84168, "timestamp": 1724164627, "title": "image.png", "url_private": "https://files.slack.com/files-pri/T04RZ2JAMM0-F07H9EQPST1/image.png?token=xoxb-REDACTED", "user": "EMPLOYEE_0026_SLACK_ID"}], "channel_info": {"id": "C05H8KVNU67", "name": "game-design", "is_private": true, "is_im": false, "is_mpim": false}, "user_profile": {"id": "EMPLOYEE_0026_SLACK_ID", "name": "Brian Foster", "real_name": "Brian Foster", "display_name": "Brian Foster", "email": "brian.foster@harmonygames.co"}, "time": "2024-08-20T14:37:15Z", "permalink": "https://harmonygamesgroup.slack.com/archives/C05H8KVNU67/p1724164635318639"}, {"ts": "1721060014.478799", "type": "message", "text": "IOS version 1393.

content.content: {"result":"{\"ok\": true, \"messages\": [{\"ts\": \"1769892718.932069\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"Simple improvement: Upgrade-adjusted difficulty multiplier (plus a tiny \\u201cskill\\u201d correction)\\nKeep your current per-level curve, but apply a multiplier based on how far a player\\u2019s upgrades are above or below the expected upgrade curve for that level. This directly addresses \\u201cahead early, stays ahead for 10+ levels.\\u201d\\n1) Compute an upgrade power score\\nUse what you already have (HP, Regen, Attack upgrades). Start linear.\\n\\u2022 `U = 0.4 * HP + 0.3 * Regen + 0.3 * Attack`\\n(Adjust weights later if Attack dominates outcomes, but start here.)\\n2) Maintain an expected upgrade curve by level\\nYou need `E[level] = expected U at this level` from either:\\ndesign intent (a table), or\\n\\u2022 median `U` from live data per level (better once you have enough data).\\n3) Convert \\u201cahead/behind\\u201d into a difficulty multiplier\\n\\u2022 `delta = U - E[level]`\\n\\u2022 `M_upg = clamp(1 + k * delta, 0.85, 1.25)`\\nWhere `k` is small (start `k = 0.05`).\\nExample using your comment \\u201c3 to 4 levels ahead\\u201d: if that maps to `delta = +2`, then `M_upg = 1.10`. That is enough to pull you back into \\u201cneed to think\\u201d without nuking average players.\\n4) Optional, still simple: a 3-bucket \\u201cskill\\u201d correction\\nThis keeps the fully-upgraded-but-crappy player from getting obliterated instantly, while still letting them struggle.\\nDefine `S` from the last 3 to 5 levels using only cheap telemetry:\\n\\u2022 attempts per level\\n\\u2022 time to clear\\n\\u2022 waves reached at death (if you have it)\\n\\u2022 number of refreshes (if relevant)\\nBucket it:\\n\\u2022 *Strong*: low attempts, fast clears\\n\\u2022 *Average*: middle\\n\\u2022 *Weak*: high attempts, slow clears\\nThen:\\n\\u2022 `M_skill = {Strong: 1.05, Average: 1.00, Weak: 0.95}`\\nFinal:\\n\\u2022 `M = M_upg * M_skill` (still clamped to 0.85 to 1.25)\\n5) Apply M to a small set of knobs only\\nDo not touch everything. Pick 2 to 3 levers that reliably create \\u201cI have to rebuild now\\u201d moments.\\nGood candidates:\\n\\u2022 enemy HP (or base health pool per wave)\\n\\u2022 enemy damage (or time-to-death pressure)\\n\\u2022 obstacle density or obstacle removal cost\\n\\u2022 shape pool entropy (only if it is a main difficulty driver, and you can change it safely)\\nExample:\\n\\u2022 `EnemyHP = BaseEnemyHP(level, wave) * M`\\n\\u2022 `EnemyDPS = BaseEnemyDPS(level, wave) * (0.5 + 0.5*M)`\\n(less aggressive than HP if DPS spikes feel unfair)\\nA/B test design\\n*Control (A)*: current level-based curve.\\n*Variant (B)*: same curve times `M` (upgrade-adjusted, plus optional skill bucket).\\nPrimary success criteria (pick 2 to avoid overfitting):\\n\\u2022 level completion rate and attempts distribution (especially levels 10 to 25)\\n\\u2022 time per level and \\u201crebuild events\\u201d frequency proxy (big board changes, silver spend spikes, obstacle removals)\\n\\u2022 D1 and D3 retention (segmented by payer vs non-payer, and by upgrade delta buckets)\\nKey segmentation to validate the exact argument in your thread:\\n\\u2022 `delta >= +2` (ahead of curve, your \\u201cspender/optimizer\\u201d proxy)\\n\\u2022 `delta between -1 and +1` (on-curve average)\\n\\u2022 `delta <= -2` (behind curve)\\nExpected outcome if this works:\\n\\u2022 ahead-of-curve players stop cruising for 10 levels, they hit meaningful rebuilds earlier (around level 11 to 12 if that\\u2019s your target)\\n\\u2022 average players stay near current difficulty\\n\\u2022 weak players still struggle, but not catastrophically earlier than today (your existing retry-based adjustments can remain as the safety net)\\nIf you want the minimum possible engineering change: implement only `M_upg` with a clamped multiplier, apply it to enemy HP only, ship the A/B. tool_use_result.content: {"result":"{\"ok\": true, \"messages\": [{\"ts\": \"1769892718.932069\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"Simple improvement: Upgrade-adjusted difficulty multiplier (plus a tiny \\u201cskill\\u201d correction)\\nKeep your current per-level curve, but apply a multiplier based on how far a player\\u2019s upgrades are above or below the expected upgrade curve for that level. This directly addresses \\u201cahead early, stays ahead for 10+ levels.\\u201d\\n1) Compute an upgrade power score\\nUse what you already have (HP, Regen, Attack upgrades). Start linear.\\n\\u2022 `U = 0.4 * HP + 0.3 * Regen + 0.3 * Attack`\\n(Adjust weights later if Attack dominates outcomes, but start here.)\\n2) Maintain an expected upgrade curve by level\\nYou need `E[level] = expected U at this level` from either:\\ndesign intent (a table), or\\n\\u2022 median `U` from live data per level (better once you have enough data).\\n3) Convert \\u201cahead/behind\\u201d into a difficulty multiplier\\n\\u2022 `delta = U - E[level]`\\n\\u2022 `M_upg = clamp(1 + k * delta, 0.85, 1.25)`\\nWhere `k` is small (start `k = 0.05`).\\nExample using your comment \\u201c3 to 4 levels ahead\\u201d: if that maps to `delta = +2`, then `M_upg = 1.10`. That is enough to pull you back into \\u201cneed to think\\u201d without nuking average players.\\n4) Optional, still simple: a 3-bucket \\u201cskill\\u201d correction\\nThis keeps the fully-upgraded-but-crappy player from getting obliterated instantly, while still letting them struggle.\\nDefine `S` from the last 3 to 5 levels using only cheap telemetry:\\n\\u2022 attempts per level\\n\\u2022 time to clear\\n\\u2022 waves reached at death (if you have it)\\n\\u2022 number of refreshes (if relevant)\\nBucket it:\\n\\u2022 *Strong*: low attempts, fast clears\\n\\u2022 *Average*: middle\\n\\u2022 *Weak*: high attempts, slow clears\\nThen:\\n\\u2022 `M_skill = {Strong: 1.05, Average: 1.00, Weak: 0.95}`\\nFinal:\\n\\u2022 `M = M_upg * M_skill` (still clamped to 0.85 to 1.25)\\n5) Apply M to a small set of knobs only\\nDo not touch everything. Pick 2 to 3 levers that reliably create \\u201cI have to rebuild now\\u201d moments.\\nGood candidates:\\n\\u2022 enemy HP (or base health pool per wave)\\n\\u2022 enemy damage (or time-to-death pressure)\\n\\u2022 obstacle density or obstacle removal cost\\n\\u2022 shape pool entropy (only if it is a main difficulty driver, and you can change it safely)\\nExample:\\n\\u2022 `EnemyHP = BaseEnemyHP(level, wave) * M`\\n\\u2022 `EnemyDPS = BaseEnemyDPS(level, wave) * (0.5 + 0.5*M)`\\n(less aggressive than HP if DPS spikes feel unfair)\\nA/B test design\\n*Control (A)*: current level-based curve.\\n*Variant (B)*: same curve times `M` (upgrade-adjusted, plus optional skill bucket).\\nPrimary success criteria (pick 2 to avoid overfitting):\\n\\u2022 level completion rate and attempts distribution (especially levels 10 to 25)\\n\\u2022 time per level and \\u201crebuild events\\u201d frequency proxy (big board changes, silver spend spikes, obstacle removals)\\n\\u2022 D1 and D3 retention (segmented by payer vs non-payer, and by upgrade delta buckets)\\nKey segmentation to validate the exact argument in your thread:\\n\\u2022 `delta >= +2` (ahead of curve, your \\u201cspender/optimizer\\u201d proxy)\\n\\u2022 `delta between -1 and +1` (on-curve average)\\n\\u2022 `delta <= -2` (behind curve)\\nExpected outcome if this works:\\n\\u2022 ahead-of-curve players stop cruising for 10 levels, they hit meaningful rebuilds earlier (around level 11 to 12 if that\\u2019s your target)\\n\\u2022 average players stay near current difficulty\\n\\u2022 weak players still struggle, but not catastrophically earlier than today (your existing retry-based adjustments can remain as the safety net)\\nIf you want the minimum possible engineering change: implement only `M_upg` with a clamped multiplier, apply it to enemy HP only, ship the A/B. That alone will tell you if upgrade variance is the real driver.\", \"channel\": \"C09UHHN6PFZ\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\", \"thread_ts\": \"1769885600.421359\", \"channel_info\": {\"id\": \"C09UHHN6PFZ\", \"name\": \"prototype\", \"is_private\": true, \"is_im\": false, \"is_mpim\": false}, \"user_profile\": {\"id\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\", \"name\": \"Leonard Hayes\", \"real_name\": \"Leonard Hayes\", \"display_name\": \"Leonard Hayes\", \"email\": \"leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co\"}, \"time\": \"2026-01-31T20:51:58Z\", \"permalink\": \"https://harmonygamesgroup.slack.com/archives/C09UHHN6PFZ/p1769892718932069?thread_ts=1769885600.421359&cid=C09UHHN6PFZ\"}, {\"ts\": \"1767769832.551599\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"I found the economy to be well balanced during my testing. Keep your current per-level curve, but apply a multiplier based on how far a player’s upgrades are above or below the expected upgrade curve for that level. This directly addresses “ahead early, stays ahead for 10+ levels.”
1) Compute an upgrade power score
Use what you already have (HP, Regen, Attack upgrades). Start linear.
• `U = 0.4 * HP + 0.3 * Regen + 0.3 * Attack`
(Adjust weights later if Attack dominates outcomes, but start here.)
2) Maintain an expected upgrade curve by level
You need `E[level] = expected U at this level` from either:
design intent (a table), or
• median `U` from live data per level (better once you have enough data).
3) Convert “ahead/behind” into a difficulty multiplier
• `delta = U - E[level]`
• `M_upg = clamp(1 + k * delta, 0.85, 1.25)`
Where `k` is small (start `k = 0.05`).
Example using your comment “3 to 4 levels ahead”: if that maps to `delta = +2`, then `M_upg = 1.10`. That is enough to pull you back into “need to think” without nuking average players.
4) Optional, still simple: a 3-bucket “skill” correction
This keeps the fully-upgraded-but-crappy player from getting obliterated instantly, while still letting them struggle.
Define `S` from the last 3 to 5 levels using only cheap telemetry:
• attempts per level
• time to clear
• waves reached at death (if you have it)
• number of refreshes (if relevant)
Bucket it:
• *Strong*: low attempts, fast clears
• *Average*: middle
• *Weak*: high attempts, slow clears
Then:
• `M_skill = {Strong: 1.05, Average: 1.00, Weak: 0.95}`
Final:
• `M = M_upg * M_skill` (still clamped to 0.85 to 1.25)
5) Apply M to a small set of knobs only
Do not touch everything. Pick 2 to 3 levers that reliably create “I have to rebuild now” moments.
Good candidates:
• enemy HP (or base health pool per wave)
• enemy damage (or time-to-death pressure)
• obstacle density or obstacle removal cost
• shape pool entropy (only if it is a main difficulty driver, and you can change it safely)
Example:
• `EnemyHP = BaseEnemyHP(level, wave) * M`
• `EnemyDPS = BaseEnemyDPS(level, wave) * (0.5 + 0.5*M)`
(less aggressive than HP if DPS spikes feel unfair)
A/B test design
*Control (A)*: current level-based curve.
*Variant (B)*: same curve times `M` (upgrade-adjusted, plus optional skill bucket).
Primary success criteria (pick 2 to avoid overfitting):
• level completion rate and attempts distribution (especially levels 10 to 25)
• time per level and “rebuild events” frequency proxy (big board changes, silver spend spikes, obstacle removals)
• D1 and D3 retention (segmented by payer vs non-payer, and by upgrade delta buckets)
Key segmentation to validate the exact argument in your thread:
• `delta >= +2` (ahead of curve, your “spender/optimizer” proxy)
• `delta between -1 and +1` (on-curve average)
• `delta <= -2` (behind curve)
Expected outcome if this works:
• ahead-of-curve players stop cruising for 10 levels, they hit meaningful rebuilds earlier (around level 11 to 12 if that’s your target)
• average players stay near current difficulty
• weak players still struggle, but not catastrophically earlier than today (your existing retry-based adjustments can remain as the safety net)
If you want the minimum possible engineering change: implement only `M_upg` with a clamped multiplier, apply it to enemy HP only, ship the A/B. ## 🧩 **Endless Mode – Engineering Summary**

### 🔧 Initial Setup

- Game starts with **40–45 sets** (a set = 3 items).
- **8 unique item types**, with size distribution:
  - 2 Large, 4 medium, 2 Small.
- Entire **item pool is defined by the designer** for each endless variant.
- Monsters also follow **30-second "tracks"**, authored by designers using level editor tools.

---

### 🔄 Refill System (Every 30 seconds)

1. **Track matched items** from the last 30 seconds.
2. **Refill those exact items** to keep total set count at 40–45.
3. Each refill is simulated and checked against a **growing Unique Item Cap**:

Refill #Time (s)Unique Cap130826093909412010.........1236014

---

### 🧠 Refill Logic Rules

1. **Simulate a refill**: Replace all matched items 1:1.
2. **Count unique items** on the new board.
3. If unique count is **below cap**:
   - Attempt to **substitute refilled items** with new unique items one-by-one.
   - After each substitution, re-check unique count.
4. If still short:
   - Remove a **fraction of total sets** = `#missingUniques / targetUniqueCap`.
   - Replace them with random sets using new unique items to reach the cap.

**Key principle:** Total number of sets never changes; only uniqueness does.

---

### 💥 New Mechanic: The Nuke (Replaces Boss Buster)

- **Builds power** by matching items:
  `NukePower += itemAttackPower × 10% × comboMultiplier`

  - If matched before timeout, combo increases.
  - Decay window shrinks by 0.25s each level (starts at 4.5s).
  - Max achievable combo: 18x.
  - The **next match** receives the combo multiplier shown.

content.text:
I've done everything Arthur asked for and replied to him in the DM thread with the three numbers: **7 still broken, 69 new tickets filed, 25 of the 28 UI children Done.**

**Which build I checked against.** I judged each bug against 0.3.310, the build players have. It came off the economy branch, which already contains everything on develop. That branch replaces Lives with Tickets and switches off Win & Collect, and that decided several outcomes.

**Linear tickets**
- Everything got moved over: 63 lines from Vincent's canvas and 7 bug posts made after it in #god-bugs, so 70 in total.
- 69 are new tickets, ENG-2438 to ENG-2506. All are on the Engineering team with the Bug label, sit under ENG-2401, and have no assignee or description. Arthur left a comment on ENG-2401 asking for "[2231]" at the front of every title, so they all have it.
  - 60 are Done (fixed).
  - 3 are Canceled: lives bugs, since Lives no longer exist in that build.
  - 6 are in Bugs (still broken): Apple sign-in, backend errors after losing a level, train level backgrounds, the nav bar disappearing after quitting a team, the megatile missing a face, and the Tile Dozer background. The Tile Dozer fix (PR #1913) was never merged.
- The last one, Android manual sign-in, is still broken but Vincent had already linked it to the open ticket ENG-2363. So I didn't file a new ticket; I added a note there with the canvas wording. Arthur's notes count it as still broken.

**UI Changes tree**
- I moved 16 open children to Done. With the 9 that were already Done, that makes 25.
- Three stay where they were:
  - ENG-2424 Collect & Win: the screen is switched off in 0.3.310.
  - ENG-2428 Season Pass: Oliver's note says the reward track still uses the old frames.
  - ENG-2437 Daily Gift: Brian's note says it never got its last pass.
- Brian's rule for closing these was in a comment on the Trello card "UI optimization pass": each ticket gets a note naming the current public build. So all 28 children now have a line saying where they landed in 0.3.310.

**Sheet.** "DD bug carry-over (Android 0.3.310)" is in your DD bug carry-over folder, with the columns Bug, Outcome, Ticket, Why. It's shared with Arthur, Robert and Oliver, the invitees on Sunday's "DD bug review", as view-only.

**Calls Arthur may want to look at**
- **Ticket titles:** Slack @-mentions in titles are written as display names (e.g. "@Arthur Blake"). Placeholder text like [PERSON_NAME_1711] is kept exactly as written.
- **What I left out:** six canvas comments whose line had been deleted, Arthur's no-ads question to Leonard, and Robert's post pointing to the QA doc.
- **Music bug:** Robert asked "intended?" but he wasn't asking Leonard, so I treated it as a bug. It's fixed in 0.3.310.
